# Ledger guests: tracking money of people without an account (design of record)

Decided with the maintainer on 2026-10-31. A ledger can hold **guests**: participants who have
no account on this server. A guest exists on exactly one ledger, is created and renamed by any
member, takes part in entries like a member, can be **locked** (the freeze without a vote), and
can later be **claimed** by someone who joins the list, so their history becomes that member's.
This is the contract the server, the web client and the Android client all implement; when it
and the code disagree, the code is wrong.

## 1. What a guest is

* A guest belongs to **one ledger** (`kind = expenses`). Nothing about a guest is visible from,
  or usable on, any other list; there is no server-wide guest registry. Shopping and checklist
  lists have no guests.
* A guest has an **id** and a **name**. The id is server-minted, `g:` + uuid4, so no guest id is
  ever an account id and both clients can tell the two apart by the prefix without a lookup.
  (`ID_MAX_LENGTH` in `sync.py` already covers the length.) The name is free text, 1..64
  characters after the server-message trim rules (`shared-test-cases/server-message.json`
  step 1), not unique on the list — two "Dave" slots are two people, rename one.
* A guest has a **locked** flag. Locked means what "voted to close" means for a member: their
  paid and owed amounts may not move while the list is open (section 4). Anyone on the list can
  set or clear it for any guest; it is a safeguard against accidental edits, not a permission.
* A guest may be **claimed** by a member (section 5). `claimed_by` is that account id, or null.
* Guests **never vote** and never count towards closing: a list closes when every current
  *member* has voted, exactly as today. A ledger can therefore close with an unsettled guest
  balance; the lock is the only protection a guest has, and that is deliberate.

## 2. Wire format

Guests are **server-maintained state on the list object**, next to `members` and `close_votes`,
outside `fields`, never client-written through `/sync`:

```json
"guests": [
  {"id": "g:…", "name": "Dave", "initials": "DA", "locked": false,
   "claimed_by": null, "created_at": 1761900000000}
]
```

Oldest first, then by id. `initials` are resolved server-side from the name (reuse the
`_default_initials` rule in `auth.py` on the name instead of the email's local part), so a
badge needs no second lookup, same as a member's. Every guest change — create, rename, lock,
unlock, remove, claim, unclaim — bumps the list's `change_seq`, so it reaches every device
through the ordinary incremental sync even though no field value moved (the T-152 mechanism).
Guests are served on every list kind as `[]` so a reader never has to special-case the key.

Guests go through their own endpoints, like votes and invites. Rationale: offline creation
through `/sync` would need a third row kind with per-field clocks; adding a guest is as rare as
inviting someone and happens while the group is together, so the endpoints are the cheaper
contract. An entry that names a guest *is* an ordinary item write and stays fully offline.

| Endpoint | Request body | Success response |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /lists/{id}/guests` | `{"name"}` | `201 {guest object}` |
| `PATCH /lists/{id}/guests/{gid}` | `{"name"?, "locked"?}` | `200 {guest object}` |
| `DELETE /lists/{id}/guests/{gid}` | — | `204` |
| `POST /lists/{id}/guests/{gid}/claim` | — | `200 {guest object}` |
| `DELETE /lists/{id}/guests/{gid}/claim` | — | `200 {guest object}` |

Errors, all after the usual `403 not_a_member` (uniform whether or not the list exists):

| Answer | When |
|---|---|
| `409 not_an_expenses_list` | any of them on another kind |
| `409 list_closed` | any of them on a closed list — the archive is read-only, guests included |
| `422 invalid_guest_name` with `field` | name blank, over 64 characters, or refused by the trim/control rules |
| `404 guest_not_found` | `gid` is not a guest of **this** list (a guest of another list is 404 here, never 403) |
| `409 guest_in_use` | `DELETE` while any **live** entry on the list names the guest (section 3) |
| `409 guest_claimed` | `PATCH {"locked"}` or `POST …/claim` on a guest that is already claimed; `DELETE …/claim` by anyone but the claimant |
| `422 voted_to_close` | `POST`/`DELETE …/claim` by a member with a close vote (claiming moves their balance; section 5) |
| `422 participant_frozen` with `account_id` | `POST …/claim` on a locked guest |

Renaming a claimed guest stays allowed (the name is still what the old entries show), and a
guest that is claimed cannot be locked: the claimant's vote now governs those numbers.

### Entries

Every key in `paid_by` / `paid_for` is one of:

* a current member's account id, or
* the id of an **unclaimed** guest of this list, or
* any id already present in the row's stored entry (unchanged: an entry naming someone who left,
  a removed guest, or a since-claimed guest stays editable).

That is the one change to `_check_expense_against_list` in `sync.py`; the shape rules are
untouched. A claimed guest id is accepted in a new entry only through the third bullet, i.e.
never — after a claim, new entries name the account. The `invalid_expense` message for an
unknown participant is reworded to say "a member or a guest of the list".

## 3. Removing a guest

`DELETE` is allowed only while no live entry on the list names the guest; otherwise
`409 guest_in_use` and the client says to edit those entries first. On success the row is hard
deleted. A tombstoned entry that still names the id is not in the way: if such an entry is ever
un-deleted by a winning write, the "already present in the stored entry" rule admits it, and the
clients render the id the way they already render a departed member (section 6). This is
exactly the former-member path, so no new client state is needed for it.

## 4. The freeze, with guests

`is_frozen(id)` in `closing.py` becomes:

* an account id: has voted, or is not a current member — unchanged;
* an unclaimed guest id: `locked`, or not (any more) a guest of this list;
* a claimed guest id: whatever `is_frozen` says for the **claimant's account** — the guest's
  numbers are that member's numbers now.

`check_write_against_freeze` is otherwise unchanged: a new row is a change from zero, a deletion
a change to zero, a type change touches everyone, and only a write that would win LWW is
checked. The error stays `422 participant_frozen` with `row_id`, `field` and the frozen id in
`account_id` (a guest id there; the key keeps its name so no client parsing changes).

"A voter changes nothing" (`voted_to_close`) is unchanged and also covers the guest endpoints:
a member who has voted may not create, rename, lock, unlock or remove a guest, since each is a
change to the list while it is open.

## 5. Claiming

Joining through an invite is unchanged on the wire: `POST /invites/redeem` makes the caller a
member. The chooser is a **client** step right after a successful redeem of an `expenses` list
whose synced list object carries unclaimed guests: "Are you one of these? — Dave / Eve / No,
I'm new". Picking one calls `POST …/claim`; "No, I'm new" does nothing. The same action is
offered on the members screen for every unclaimed guest ("This is me"), so someone who
dismissed the chooser, or a member who was already on the list when the slot was created, can
claim later. No invite is ever tied to a guest.

Claiming records `claimed_by` and bumps `change_seq`; **no stored entry is rewritten**. Rewriting
map keys inside items would fight field-level LWW and stale offline writes; the alias avoids it.
Both clients fold a claimed guest into the claimant for every figure:

* `effectiveId(id) = guests[id].claimed_by ?? id`, applied to every key of every entry before
  the per-participant sums in `expense-arithmetic.json` are taken;
* balances, settle-up, "net spent" and the per-entry effect are computed on effective ids;
* an entry row still shows the guest's name where the stored key is the guest id (that is what
  was written), but the balance and settle-up rows show only the member.

An account may claim more than one guest on a list (two slots that were both Dave); the fold is
a plain map, so nothing special-cases it. A claim is reversible by the claimant alone while the
list is open (`DELETE …/claim`), which puts the alias back to a plain guest; after the list
closes it is final, like everything else on the archive.

A claim is refused when the claimant has voted (`voted_to_close`) or the guest is locked
(`participant_frozen`), since it moves the claimant's balance by the guest's. Leaving the list
is impossible while it is open (`list_open`, unchanged); when the claimant leaves a closed list,
or deletes their account, the claim stays as history and the clients render the account the way
they already render a former member.

## 6. Clients, both alike

* **Names.** A participant id resolves to: a current member → initials/email as today; an
  unclaimed guest → its name with a guest marker (an outline badge and "guest" in the
  accessible label); a claimed guest, wherever a stored key still is one → the guest's name
  with the claimant's initials ("Dave → DP"); an id that is neither → "Former member N" exactly
  as today, so T-197's numbering rule covers removed guests without a second rule.
* **Members screen** gains a Guests section: the list, an Add guest field, and per guest:
  rename, lock/unlock toggle with a one-line explanation ("Locked: amounts cannot change, like
  a member who agreed to close"), remove (disabled with the reason while in use), and "This is
  me" while unclaimed. A claimed guest shows "claimed by DP" and no toggle.
* **Entry form** offers members and unclaimed guests as participants, guests marked; a locked
  guest is shown the way a voter is shown today (amount fixed, see T-196 for the equal-split
  trap, which must not zero a locked guest either).
* **Balances** show guests like members, marked; a locked guest carries the same "amounts
  fixed" line a voter does (T-203's wording must not say "agreed to close" for a guest — a
  separate string).
* **After redeem**: the chooser above, on both clients, only for an expenses list with
  unclaimed guests. Android's multi-account "Join with which account?" comes first; the guest
  chooser follows the join.
* **Rejections**: `guest_in_use`, `guest_claimed`, `guest_not_found`, `invalid_guest_name` get
  rows in `web/src/i18n/apiErrors.ts`, Android's `ErrorText.kt` and the wire-contract table.
  `participant_frozen` wording on both clients says "locked guest" when the id is a guest.
* **Strings** in all ten locales on both clients, paired by `crossClient.test.ts`.
* **Android**: `guests` is persisted on the list entity (Room migration), `effectiveId` and the
  fold live in `:core` next to the balance arithmetic, the new API calls in `Api.kt`, any new
  class in the Koin modules.
* **Gating**: every guest control is shown only when the account's `serverProtocol` is at or
  above the version below; against an older server the ledger looks as it does today.

## 7. Shared cases

`shared-test-cases/expense-arithmetic.json` gets a `guests` block: entries keyed by guest ids,
mixed with members; a claimed guest whose key is folded into the claimant; two guests claimed
by one account; a removed guest rendered as former. Both clients run them, and the sum-to-zero
property test runs over guest ids too.

## 8. Protocol

This is a protocol change: `PROTOCOL_VERSION` 3 → 4, so the release that ships it is a major
one. A protocol-3 client receiving a guest id in an entry would render a live guest as a former
member and could not add one, and a claimed guest would appear as a stranger with a balance of
their own; that is the "cannot handle correctly" the versioning rule names. Both clients keep
`MIN_SERVER_PROTOCOL` where it is. Changelog row in `docs/wire-contract.md` "Protocol version".

## 9. Not in this design

* Guests on shopping or checklist lists ("assigned to") — no.
* Server-wide or cross-list guests, guest contact details, a guest's own view of the ledger.
* Invites that name a guest.
* Merging two guests into one, or a guest into a *former* member.

## Implementation tickets (to file when work starts, as for T-239)

server (schema `guests` table, endpoints, participant rule, freeze, housekeeping checks, GC with
the list, protocol 4) · web (data layer, fold, members screen, form, balances, chooser, strings)
· Android (Room, `:core` fold, API, screens, chooser, strings) · shared cases · release.
title: Ledger guests: participants without an account — add, lock, claim on join (design)
